intro: Aeroplan "Experiences" isn't one tidy storefront - it's two real things wearing the same hat. One: you can spend Aeroplan points on activities, tours and travel experiences through the Aeroplan eStore and Air Canada Vacations. Two: if you carry the right Amex Aeroplan card, you get cardholder access to Front Of The Line presales and curated members-only events. Points-first flexibility on one side, VIP access on the other.
what_you_get:
Two distinct lanes:

**Redeem points for experiences**
- Activities and travel experiences, tours, and excursions (concerts, museums, nature/sightseeing) through Air Canada Vacations
- Cruises and vacation packages bundled with flights and hotels
- Merchandise and retailer gift cards via the Aeroplan eStore

**Cardholder event access (Amex Aeroplan cards)**
- Front Of The Line Amex Presale and Reserved Tickets to in-demand concerts, theatre, festivals and select racing events - often before the general public
- Curated members-only events: unique dining experiences, virtual parties, special online shopping moments
how_it_works:
It depends which lane you're in:

- **Points redemptions** are priced in Aeroplan points (or points + cash). You book experiences, tours and packages through Air Canada Vacations, or grab activities, merch and gift cards on the Aeroplan eStore. Standard fixed redemption - no bidding.
- **Cardholder access** is a presale mechanic, not a points spend. Front Of The Line gives Amex cardmembers a window to buy presale or reserved tickets before (or after) general release, paid in full on your Amex card. Curated cardmember events are invitation/access based.
how_to_access:
- **Points redemptions** are open to any Aeroplan member - just sign in at the Aeroplan eStore or Air Canada Vacations.
- **Front Of The Line presales** require an eligible American Express card; the richest access sits with the American Express Aeroplan Reserve Card, which also unlocks the curated Cardmember Exclusive Events. Subscribe to the Front Of The Line entertainment e-updates to get listings emailed to you.
- Note: the Amex Aeroplan cards and Front Of The Line are Canadian products - this access is geared to Canada-based cardholders.
standout_examples: Inventory rotates constantly, but the real categories are consistent. On the points side: tours, sightseeing and activity packages through Air Canada Vacations, plus cruises and flight-and-hotel bundles. On the Amex access side: Front Of The Line presales to in-demand concerts, theatre runs, music festivals and select racing events, plus curated cardmember moments - past examples have included a Valentine's dining package and an exclusive virtual art experience. Specific live listings change, so check the eStore and your Amex Experiences feed for what's bookable right now.
good_to_know:
- Front Of The Line presales and curated cardmember events are tied to eligible Amex cards (best on the Aeroplan Reserve) and are a Canadian benefit.
- Presale tickets are paid in full on your Amex card - this is ticket access, not a points discount. Quantities are limited and hot events sell out fast.
- Experience/tour redemptions run through Air Canada Vacations and the eStore; refundability and change rules follow the individual operator's and Air Canada Vacations' terms - read them before you book.
- Find points inventory at the Aeroplan eStore and vacations.aircanada.com; find event access via Amex Experiences and the Front Of The Line e-updates.
value_take: Worth knowing on both fronts: the points lane gives you flexible ways to burn Aeroplan points beyond flights, and the Amex Reserve lane is genuine VIP access - presale shots at concerts and events the general public can't touch yet. Just know which one you're using, because only one of them actually spends points.
requires_card: Eligible American Express Aeroplan cards (Front Of The Line)

intro: Flying Blue Experiences is Air France-KLM's newest way to burn Miles on something other than a plane seat - launched in January 2026, it lets members redeem Miles for premium access to concerts and major sporting events. Think VIP boxes at marquee Paris venues, not a flight to Paris. It's small and France-centric for now, but the access is genuinely the kind of thing that's hard to buy outright.
what_you_get:
The platform launched focused on premium live-event hospitality, with more categories promised over time:
- **Concerts** - VIP box seats for shows at top Paris venues
- **Major sporting events** - including marquee fixtures like the Six Nations rugby opener
- **VIP hospitality** - access is via 16-seat private boxes at the Accor Arena and the Stade de France, so you're getting a premium vantage point, not nosebleeds
- Air France-KLM has said other experience types will be added gradually, so expect the menu to grow beyond Paris concerts and sports.
how_it_works: Straightforward fixed-price Miles redemption - no bidding, no auctions. You browse the Flying Blue Store, pick an available event, and pay a set number of Miles per ticket. For example, the France vs England Six Nations rugby match listed at 60,000 Miles per ticket (so a pair runs you 120,000). Pricing is per seat, and inventory is tied to specific dated events, so it's book-it-when-you-see-it, not an always-on catalog.
how_to_access: Open to all Flying Blue members - no elite status or specific co-brand card required to redeem. Status does add a perk, though: members at Silver tier and above get fast-lane entry to every event at the Accor Arena (worth roughly 30-45 minutes saved per event). You just need a Flying Blue account and enough Miles. US members can earn Miles via Air France-KLM co-brand and transferable-points partners (Amex, Chase, Citi, Bilt, Capital One all transfer to Flying Blue), then redeem on the Store.
standout_examples: At launch the headliner was the Six Nations Championship opener, France vs England, at the Stade de France - VIP box seating for 60,000 Miles per ticket. Beyond that, the Accor Arena and Stade de France each carry around ten concerts and sporting events in a 16-seat VIP box format. Specific listings rotate with the live-event calendar, so check the Store for what's currently bookable.
good_to_know: This is a brand-new, deliberately limited offering - around ten events per venue, both in Paris, so it's really aimed at members who can get to France. Cancellation, change and refund terms are spelled out per-event in the T&Cs you see during booking, and Air France-KLM has flagged that the policy reflects the premium, scarce nature of the seats - read those before you commit, because rare-inventory tickets are rarely flexible. Pricing is quoted per seat, so double the Miles if you want to bring someone. Find inventory on the Flying Blue Store under Experiences.
value_take: Worth knowing because it turns Miles into access you genuinely can't easily buy - private VIP boxes at the Stade de France and Accor Arena - and the fixed pricing means no auction guesswork. Just keep in mind it's Paris-only and tiny for now, so it's a treat for members already heading to France, not a reason to chase Miles.

intro: American AAdvantage Experiences is really two things wearing one hat: AAdvantage Events, an everyday Ticketmaster-powered marketplace where you can spend or earn AAdvantage miles on concerts, sports, theater and comedy, and a rotating set of exclusive, miles-only opportunities like FIFA World Cup 26 match tickets and Mastercard Priceless cardholder auctions. If you have an AAdvantage stash and a calendar full of live events, this is a legit way to put those miles to work without booking a flight.
what_you_get:
- **Live event tickets (AAdvantage Events):** Concerts, sports games, theater, and comedy via Ticketmaster - millions of standard and verified-resale listings.
- **Marquee sports access:** Miles-redeemable tickets to big-ticket events like the FIFA World Cup 26, plus matches and tournaments such as U.S. Soccer and PGA Championship dates.
- **Mastercard Priceless experiences:** AAdvantage Mastercard cardholders get access to curated culinary, sporting, and luxury experiences, including miles auctions (for example, a private Boeing 787 flight-simulator session).
- **Points-or-cash flexibility:** Pay with miles, cash, or a blend - and earn miles plus Loyalty Points when you pay cash.
how_it_works:
Three different mechanics depending on the experience:
- **AAdvantage Events (fixed price, points-or-cash):** Shop at aadvantageevents.com. Pay fully with miles, fully with cash, or combine the two in 1,000-mile increments. Cash purchases earn 1 mile and 1 Loyalty Point per $1 on standard and resale tickets (excluding taxes and fees); any ticket paid partly with miles earns nothing.
- **Exclusive miles redemptions (fixed price, tiered access):** Limited drops like FIFA World Cup 26 are miles-only, sold as sets of 2 tickets at fixed mile prices that can rise between phases as inventory tightens.
- **Mastercard Priceless auctions (binding bid):** Cardholder auctions where you bid miles - highest bid wins and bids are binding.
how_to_access: AAdvantage Events is open to any AAdvantage member - log in with your number at aadvantageevents.com, and members with elite status or an AAdvantage co-branded credit card use fewer miles when signed in. Exclusive drops like FIFA World Cup 26 grant early-access windows by elite tier (ConciergeKey and Executive Platinum first, then Platinum Pro / Platinum / Gold, then all members). Mastercard Priceless experiences and miles auctions are gated to AAdvantage Mastercard cardholders (Citi and Barclays AAdvantage cards).
standout_examples: Inventory rotates, but recent real highlights include: FIFA World Cup 26 - members could redeem miles for tickets to all 104 matches, sold in sets of 2, with the Mexico City opener starting around 435,000 miles and the final near 1,200,000 miles. On the auction side, a Mastercard Priceless lot offered a private 4-hour Boeing 787 flight-simulator session at American's Fort Worth Skyview campus with a Thompson Dallas stay, with bids running into the hundreds of thousands of miles. Day to day, AAdvantage Events lists everyday concerts, comedy, theater, and sports through Ticketmaster.
good_to_know: AAdvantage Events runs on Ticketmaster, so pricing and purchase protection mirror Ticketmaster's - only verified standard and resale tickets are bookable (non-verified resale is grayed out). Mile-blended tickets do not earn miles or Loyalty Points; only fully-cash purchases earn. Event tickets generally follow the venue/event refund rules (typically non-refundable unless an event is canceled or rescheduled), and auctions are binding - no take-backs. Big drops like the World Cup are time-boxed with tiered access windows, so set a reminder. Find everything at aadvantageevents.com; Priceless experiences live under the Mastercard Priceless cardholder portal.
value_take: Worth knowing for the flexibility and access: you can offload miles on events you'd buy anyway, and elites/cardholders get exclusive early shots at hard-to-get tickets like the World Cup. Treat the headline mile prices on marquee drops with eyes open, but the points-or-cash optionality and earn-on-cash angle make this a genuinely useful corner of AAdvantage.

intro: Atmos Rewards Unlocked (formerly Mileage Plan Unlocked) is Alaska and Hawaiian's experiences marketplace where points - not cash - are the only way in. Think Coachella passes, stadium suites, Napa dinners, and bucket-list getaways, all bookable with the same miles you'd otherwise burn on flights. It is a genuinely different way to use a balance, and some of these experiences you literally cannot buy any other way.
what_you_get:
Curated, points-only access to experiences across several categories:
- **Music and festivals** - passes to events like Coachella and Stagecoach
- **Sports** - exclusive access to Alaska Airlines / Atmos suites at games and concerts (food and drinks often included)
- **Culinary** - chef dinners and food-and-wine experiences, including events with Pacific Northwest chefs
- **Travel and getaways** - curated trips to destinations like Alaska and Guatemala, plus hotel-and-activity packages
- **Entertainment** - comedy shows, theater, and other one-of-a-kind outings

Inventory rotates and spans 15-plus markets, so the live lineup changes regularly.
how_it_works:
Two redemption mechanics, both paid entirely in points:

- **Buy-it-now** - many experiences carry a published points price; redeem and the experience unlocks instantly.
- **Auctions** - premium items are auctioned. Alaska sets the opening bid, increments, and duration; you bid points while the auction is live, and the highest bidder wins.

Entry points start as low as 10,000 miles. Points are deducted at time of purchase (or auction close). After you book, you get a confirmation email and a team member or partner follows up with details - allow roughly 7-10 business days for fulfillment.
how_to_access: Open to all Atmos Rewards (formerly Mileage Plan) members - no special credit card or elite tier required to browse or redeem. HawaiianMiles members must first transfer their HawaiianMiles into Mileage Plan / Atmos miles to redeem. No card gating, though hitting milestone tiers can earn perks like an Unlocked discount code (for example, members have received a sizable miles-off code at the MVP Gold 100K milestone).
standout_examples: Recently featured items have included passes to Coachella and Stagecoach, exclusive access to Alaska Airlines suites at sporting events and concerts, a getaway to Guatemala, and dinner at a renowned Napa restaurant. One concrete published example: roughly 10,000 points for access to the Atmos Suite at T-Mobile Park in Seattle for a Mariners game, with food and drinks included. Inventory rotates constantly, so treat these as a flavor of what shows up rather than a permanent menu.
good_to_know: Big catch: redemptions are nonrefundable - points are deducted at purchase (or auction close) and you don't get them back even if you can't attend. Auction bids are final and cannot be lowered or withdrawn, and you must hold the bid amount in your account when you bid and when the auction closes. Buying miles? Allow 24-48 hours before they're usable here. Browse live inventory at unlocked.atmosrewards.com (formerly unlocked.alaskaair.com); availability is concentrated in major US markets, so geography matters for the event-based items.
value_take: Worth knowing because it turns an airline balance into access you often can't buy with cash - festival passes, stadium suites, chef dinners - with a low 10,000-point entry. Just go in clear-eyed: it's nonrefundable and auctions are binding, so only bid points you're truly ready to part with.

intro: British Airways runs two very different "experiences" plays for Avios collectors, and it's worth knowing which is which. One is BA Club Live - members-only access to concerts and shows at the new British Airways ARC venue at Olympia in London, with tickets ringfenced just for The British Airways Club. The other is the everyday "Spend Avios on Experiences" rail, where you redeem points (or points-plus-cash) for attractions, tours, spa days and theme-park tickets through the Avios app or ba.com.
what_you_get:
Two distinct tracks:

**BA Club Live (access):** Exclusive, ringfenced ticket allocations to concerts and shows at British Airways ARC, a 3,800-capacity venue at Olympia, London that opened in June 2026. Tickets are reserved for Club members and booked through a dedicated member portal. Some tickets include access to the British Airways Wing VIP lounge - a dedicated cocktail bar and, for select shows, a private balcony over the stage.

**Spend Avios on Experiences (redeem):** Bookable attractions and activities in major cities worldwide - sightseeing tours, walking tours, cooking classes, dinner cruises, arts and culture - plus UK-focused options like attractions, spa days, theme-park entry and Disneyland Paris tickets.
how_it_works:
**BA Club Live:** Access-only. You don't bid or redeem Avios for the show ticket itself - Club members get a ringfenced allocation and buy through a dedicated portal after logging in to your BA account. Allocations are limited, so it's first-in for popular shows. Bonus: from June 2026 you can also collect 10 Avios per GBP 1 at select bars and restaurants across Olympia when you attend.

**Spend Avios on Experiences:** Fixed-price redemption with flexibility - book on the Avios app or via the "Book Experiences" link on the Spending Avios page at ba.com, and pay with Avios, cash, or a mix of both. Pricing is set per experience, similar to how hotels and car hire work in the Avios ecosystem.
how_to_access: Both tracks require membership in The British Airways Club (the renamed Executive Club). Joining is free and open to anyone. For BA Club Live, log in to your BA account to see what's on and access the member ticket allocation; some British Airways Wing VIP perks are reserved for select (higher) Club tiers. No specific credit card is required, though UK BA American Express cardholders (British Airways Amex and Premium Plus) are a common way to build the Avios balance you'd spend.
standout_examples: British Airways ARC opened on 16 June 2026 with a performance from Self Esteem, followed by a lineup including McFly and Van Morrison - all with Club-member ticket allocations. On the redeem side, recurring categories include UK theme-park tickets, spa days, Disneyland Paris entry, and city tours and cooking classes worldwide. Specific live inventory rotates constantly, so treat these as representative of the categories rather than fixed offers.
good_to_know: Find BA Club Live shows by logging in to your BA account; find redeemable experiences via the Avios app or the "Book Experiences" link on ba.com's Spending Avios page. Refundability varies by experience and by show - check the specific terms before booking, as event tickets are often non-refundable. The redeemable experiences catalog is UK and Europe-heavy, and BA Club Live is physically tied to London's Olympia, so this is most useful if you travel to or live in the UK. On value: points-pundits note Avios on third-party experiences typically returns less than flight redemptions, so lean on the points-or-cash flexibility and only spend Avios when the cash price stings or you have surplus points.
value_take: Worth knowing for two reasons: BA Club Live is genuine money-can't-buy access - ringfenced seats at a brand-new London venue you can't get as a non-member - and the Spend Avios on Experiences rail gives you points-or-cash flexibility to knock down the price of a spa day, theme-park ticket or city tour.

intro: SkyMiles Experiences is Delta's redemption playground for the stuff a regular award ticket can't get you - dinner at The French Laundry, a wellness retreat, courtside-level access, even riding the Delta float at WorldPride. You spend SkyMiles (sometimes by outright "Redeem Now" purchase, often by bidding in an auction) on curated once-in-a-lifetime events instead of flights. Fresh inventory drops every other Tuesday, so it's worth a peek if you're sitting on a SkyMiles pile and want something memorable.
what_you_get:
Curated experiences organized into rotating collections:

- **Music & Film** - concerts, premieres, and entertainment access
- **Culinary** - chef dinners, kitchen tours, prix-fixe tastings with wine pairings
- **Sports** - games, events, and athlete-adjacent access
- **Wellness & Adventure** - multi-night retreats and active escapes
- **Fashion, Art & Design** - private styling appointments, shopping credits, design events
- **Card Member Collection** - experiences reserved for eligible Delta SkyMiles American Express Card Members

Many are packaged with extras like round-trip flights, hotel stays, and a guest spot, so you're often redeeming for a full trip, not just a single ticket.
how_it_works:
Two ways to redeem with SkyMiles:

- **Redeem Now** - buy select experiences outright for a fixed miles price, first come first served.
- **Bid** - place a miles bid (in 1,000-mile increments) on an auction-style experience. Highest bid when the auction closes wins. If you're outbid or don't win, your miles are returned to your account. If you win, Delta's team reaches out to coordinate the details for you and your guests.

There's no points-or-cash toggle here - it's a SkyMiles redemption platform. New experiences are added on Tuesdays, every two weeks.
how_to_access: Open to any Delta SkyMiles Member who is 18 or older and resides in the 50 US states or DC. You'll need to be logged into your SkyMiles account to bid or redeem. No elite status or co-brand card is required for the general collections - your SkyMiles balance is the only gate. The exception is the **Card Member Collection**, which is reserved for eligible Basic Delta SkyMiles American Express Card Members (additional/authorized card members don't qualify).
standout_examples: Recently featured (inventory rotates, so treat these as a flavor sample, not a standing menu): a 7-night Los Cabos vacation with Exclusive Resorts (bidding had climbed past 400,000 miles); riding the Delta boat at WorldPride Amsterdam with a hotel stay and round-trip flights; dinner and a kitchen tour at The French Laundry in Yountville, CA; a 6-night all-inclusive wellness retreat at The Ranch Malibu; an intimate chef's dinner at MIDA in Boston with James Beard winner Douglass Williams; and a private styling appointment with a $1,500 credit at Revolve & FWRD in LA.
good_to_know: All wins and Redeem Now purchases are final - no mileage refunds, and resale is prohibited. The big catch: bids are binding, so only bid an amount of miles you're genuinely willing to part with. Miles for losing or outbid auctions are returned automatically. You must be 18+ and live in the 50 states or DC to participate. Browse and filter inventory by category, location, and miles range at skymilesexperiences.com; new drops land every other Tuesday and many experiences are explicitly limited availability.
value_take: If you've got a stash of SkyMiles and have already covered your flight redemptions, this is a legitimately fun way to spend them on access you genuinely can't buy off the shelf. Just go in clear-eyed: bids are binding and there's no cash-out, so it's a "spend miles I'd otherwise sit on" play, not a value-maximizing one.
refundable: No - wins and purchases are binding (losing bids refunded)

intro: Skywards Exclusives is Emirates' experiences marketplace where you spend (or bid) Skywards Miles instead of cash on the airline's massive sponsorship portfolio - think Wimbledon, Formula One Paddock Club, Arsenal hospitality and the odd money-can't-buy moment. You either Buy Now at a fixed Miles price or throw your hat in a SkyBid auction. It's a genuinely fun way to burn Miles you'd otherwise sit on, as long as you go in knowing the catches.
what_you_get:
Curated experiences pulled from Emirates' global sponsorships, redeemable with Miles:

- **Sports** across 11 disciplines - football, motorsports (F1), tennis, cricket, rugby, golf, horseracing, baseball, sailing, cycling and Aussie Rules - from general-admission tickets to VIP hospitality suites
- **Concerts and live performances** at venues like Dubai's Coca-Cola Arena
- **Money-can't-buy experiences** and exclusive VIP invitations
- **Signed memorabilia** - jerseys and balls from legendary clubs
- Inventory rotates: Emirates says roughly 48 events were offered across the prior 12 months
how_it_works:
Two redemption mechanics on exclusives.skywards.com or the Emirates App:

- **Buy Now** - a fixed Miles price; your Miles are debited instantly in exchange for the listed item.
- **Auctions (SkyBid)** - you bid Miles against other members. A maximum-bid feature auto-bids in increments to keep you in the lead up to a cap you set, even while offline. If anyone bids in the final 60 seconds, the clock extends another 60 seconds until activity stops.

Winning bidder pays at auction close - the winning Miles amount is deducted automatically, and you must have sufficient Miles in your account at that moment.
how_to_access: Open to any enrolled Emirates Skywards member aged 18+ who agrees to the Programme Rules - no minimum elite tier to use the platform generally. That said, individual listings can carry tier restrictions: some premium experiences are reserved for Gold and Platinum members, and a handful for Platinum only. No co-brand credit card is required.
standout_examples:
Recently featured items (inventory rotates):

- **Formula One Paddock Club** access from around 150,000 Miles
- **Arsenal** home matches - general admission from about 10,000 Miles, hospitality suite from about 60,000 Miles
- **ICC Men's T20 World Cup** match tickets from about 3,000 Miles
- **Signed football memorabilia** (jerseys, balls) from legendary clubs from about 52,000 Miles
- Past marquee events include Wimbledon, Roland Garros, the US Open and the FA Cup
good_to_know: Miles redemptions here are non-refundable, non-cancellable and non-transferable, and items are non-exchangeable with no cash alternative - so be sure before you commit. Auction bids are final the second you submit them: they can't be withdrawn or lowered, and the anti-snipe 60-second extension means a "closing" auction can run on. Inventory is event-driven and geographically skewed toward Emirates' sponsorship calendar (heavy UK, Europe and UAE), so US-based members may find fewer local options. Browse current listings on exclusives.skywards.com or in the Emirates App.
value_take: It's one of the more interesting non-flight uses of Miles - real access to events and hospitality you can't easily buy, with the flexibility to spend Miles instead of cash. Worth a look before your Miles expire, just go in clear-eyed: redemptions are binding and inventory leans toward Emirates' sponsorship cities.

intro: Miles & More Experiences (the program's "event awards") lets Lufthansa Group loyalty members spend miles on exclusive cultural, culinary, and sporting events across Europe instead of cashing them in for flights. Think opera nights at Frankfurt's Alte Oper, productions at the Arena di Verona, gourmet menus, and up-close motorsport - each bundled with member-only extras. It is a rotating, access-flavored use for miles that would otherwise just buy economy seats.
what_you_get:
The event awards portfolio rotates but consistently spans three lanes:

- **Cultural** - concert evenings at Frankfurt's Alte Oper and world-famous opera at the Arena di Verona, plus other performances.
- **Culinary** - haute cuisine and gourmet menus, plus curated sommelier/wine tastings.
- **Sporting** - motorsport racing experienced up close and chances to meet top sporting legends.

Every event comes with "that little bit extra" - exclusive guided tours, catering, and other member-only touches built into the package.
how_it_works: It is a **fixed-miles redemption**, not an auction. You browse the live event highlights on the Miles & More site, pick one that is currently available, and pay with your miles - "only your miles make participation possible." Each listing shows its own mile price (inventory and pricing rotate by event). Across the wider program, Cash & Miles lets you top up with euros if you are short, though core event pricing is mile-based. Many packages let you bring up to three additional family members or friends on the same redemption.
how_to_access: Open to **all Miles & More members** - no elite tier or specific co-brand card required. Membership is free to join on the Miles & More site, and the program is the loyalty scheme for Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian, Brussels Airlines, and other Lufthansa Group carriers. You just need a mile balance and an account; browse and book the event awards directly while logged in.
standout_examples:
Specific listings rotate, but recurring marquee categories on the official events page include:

- Concert evenings at the **Alte Oper Frankfurt**.
- World-famous opera productions at the **Arena di Verona**.
- Up-close **motorsport** experiences and meet-and-greets with sporting legends.
- **Haute cuisine** gourmet menus and sommelier-led tastings.

Treat any single title as inventory-dependent - check the live page for what is bookable now.
good_to_know: Inventory is a rotating set of "highlights currently available," so the catalog changes - check back rather than expecting a fixed menu. Events skew heavily European (Frankfurt, Verona, and other Lufthansa Group home markets), which matters if you are redeeming from the US. intro: Qantas turns Frequent Flyer points into more than just flights through Points Exclusives - a rotating shop of money-can't-buy experiences, VIP packages, and collectibles you redeem with points. There are two flavors here: fixed-price experiences you book outright, and periodic Points Auctions where members bid their points against each other for one-of-a-kind prizes. If you are sitting on a big Qantas balance, this is how you spend it on something memorable instead of a saver economy seat.
what_you_get:
Qantas Points Exclusives and Points Auctions have featured a rotating mix:
- Money-can't-buy experiences (chef dinners in the Qantas First lounge, scenic flights, behind-the-scenes aviation access like a Dreamliner simulator)
- Sports and concert VIP packages (premium seats, pregame access, meet-and-greets)
- Luxury travel bundles (business-class tickets paired with five-star hotel stays)
- Aviation collectibles and memorabilia (retired A380 SkyBed seats, bar carts, crockery)
- Lifestyle and tech items via the broader Qantas Marketplace
Inventory rotates constantly - the auction drops new lots on a schedule, and Exclusives refresh periodically.
how_it_works:
Two mechanics run side by side:
- **Points Exclusives (fixed price):** experiences and packages listed at a set points cost. You redeem points to book outright - first come, first served while stock lasts.
- **Points Auctions (bidding):** Qantas loads exclusive lots and members bid their points against each other over a set window. Highest bid wins, and winning bids are binding - you are committing your points, so do not bid more than you are willing to part with.
Some Marketplace items also support Points Plus Pay, letting you split the cost between points and a card.
how_to_access: Open to all Qantas Frequent Flyer members - no specific co-brand card or elite tier required. You just need an active membership and enough points in your account. Access Points Exclusives and the Points Auction through the Qantas Marketplace / Frequent Flyer site when you are logged in. Note this is an Australia-centric program, so the richest inventory and event access skews toward Australia.
standout_examples: Past featured items show the range: a five-course Neil Perry chef dinner with wines in the Sydney First Class lounge for a group; an Antarctica scenic flight for two departing an Australian city; a Boeing 787 Dreamliner flight-simulator session; retired A380 business-class SkyBed seats sold as collectibles; and VIP sports packages such as an NBA game bundle with premium seats, pregame warm-up access, a personalized jersey, and an on-court photo. These are illustrative - actual inventory rotates, so check the live listings for what is currently available.
good_to_know: Auction bids are binding - if you win, those points are committed, so bid deliberately. Inventory is heavily Australia-focused (experiences, events, and travel often depart or take place there), which is the main catch for US-based members. Refundability and cancellation terms vary by experience and are spelled out in each listing's terms - read them before you commit. Find current inventory by logging into the Qantas Frequent Flyer / Marketplace site and browsing Points Exclusives or the active Points Auction; the auction runs as periodic timed events rather than always-on.
value_take: Worth knowing if you hold a large Qantas balance and want access to genuine money-can't-buy moments - chef dinners, aviation experiences, VIP event packages - rather than letting points idle. The auction format also gives savvy members a shot at one-of-a-kind prizes that simply are not for sale any other way.

intro: The Privilege Club Collection is Qatar Airways' answer to "what else can I do with Avios besides flights?" - an online marketplace where members spend (or bid) Avios on VIP event tickets, fan experiences, and limited-edition memorabilia. Think Formula 1 Paddock Club, pitchside football, O2 concerts, and the occasional money-can't-quite-buy moment, all priced in points instead of cash.
what_you_get:
Access leans heavily into Qatar Airways' sponsorship portfolio, sorted into two broad lanes:

- **Sports and leisure** - Formula 1 Paddock Club VIP hospitality, pitchside and VIP football (Paris Saint-Germain, Inter Milan, UEFA Champions League), rugby (United Rugby Championship), and cricket (Royal Challengers Bangalore). Mega events like the FIFA World Cup 2026 have also appeared.
- **Music and culture** - VIP concert tickets, frequently at London's O2 Arena (past lineups have featured names like John Mayer, Depeche Mode, Liam Gallagher, and the Jonas Brothers).
- **Memorabilia and limited-edition items** - signed and collectible merchandise tied to those same teams and events.

Inventory rotates constantly as Qatar's sponsorship calendar shifts, so the exact lineup changes month to month.
how_it_works:
Two redemption mechanics live side by side on the Collection platform:

- **Buy now (fixed price)** - listed for a set number of Avios; pay it and it's yours, first come first served.
- **Auction (bid)** - you bid Avios against other members. The full bid amount is deducted and held in escrow; if you're outbid, it's refunded back to your account. An anti-sniping rule extends the clock by 60 seconds whenever a bid lands in the final minute. Win the auction and the Avios are spent - that part is binding.

Everything is points-only on the Collection itself (no points-or-cash split here), though Qatar separately lets you part-pay flights, upgrades, and Duty Free with Avios.
how_to_access: Open to Privilege Club members, but you generally need to be the **Main Member** (the primary account holder) to bid on or buy experiences. There's no specific co-brand card or elite tier required to browse and redeem - any Avios balance gets you in. You'll need enough Avios to cover the buy-now price or place a competitive bid, and inventory/pricing can vary by region (the US, UK, and other storefronts list separately at collection.qatarairways.com).
standout_examples: Recurring headliners include **Formula 1 Paddock Club** VIP hospitality packages across the F1 season, and **UEFA Champions League** matchday packages with pitchside warmup viewing and Champions Club hospitality. Club football regularly features **Paris Saint-Germain** and **Inter Milan**, and O2 Arena concert tickets have surfaced for major touring artists. Because these track Qatar's live sponsorships, treat any specific listing as a rotating drop rather than a permanent fixture.
good_to_know: Find inventory at collection.qatarairways.com (pick your region storefront). Auction bids are held in escrow and refunded if you're outbid, but a winning bid or buy-now purchase commits the Avios - assume completed redemptions are non-refundable unless a listing says otherwise. Availability is region-specific and heavily skewed toward Qatar-sponsored teams and venues, so the catalog reflects their deals, not the whole sports/music world. Many marquee experiences exclude flights and travel - read each listing for what's actually included.
value_take: It's one of the more genuinely interesting non-flight uses of Avios - real VIP access to F1, top-flight football, and arena concerts that are otherwise hard to get, with the flexibility to either lock in a fixed price or chase a deal at auction. Worth a look before your Avios just sit there, especially if a sponsored team or venue you already love shows up.
refundable: Bids refunded if outbid; wins are binding

intro: MileagePlus Exclusives is United's marketplace for spending your miles on experiences instead of flights - think courtside seats, chef's tables, Broadway, and behind-the-scenes airline access. Some items have a fixed "buy now" miles price, but a lot of the good stuff goes to auction, so you bid your miles and the highest bidder wins. It is points-first by design: miles are the currency, not a cash add-on.
what_you_get:
Six rotating categories, all priced in MileagePlus miles:
- **Travel** - global excursions tied to United's route network.
- **Sports** - tickets and premium-club seating for MLB, NBA, NHL, NFL, WNBA, PGA TOUR, plus VIP facility and talent access (e.g. batting practice with a team).
- **Culinary & Dining** - private and multi-course chef's-table dinners with notable culinary talent.
- **Arts & Culture** - Broadway, ballet, theater, and independent film.
- **Entertainment** - concerts, festivals, comedy, TV tapings, and studio tours.
- **Uniquely United** - behind-the-scenes airline experiences (flight simulator, ops facilities) you can't get anywhere else.
how_it_works:
Three formats run side by side:
- **Buy now** - a fixed miles price; redeem and it's yours while it lasts.
- **Auction** - place a bid in miles; the system auto-bids up to the max you set, and you may win for less than your max. Win and it's a **legally binding contract** - miles are debited automatically, and you cannot retract or lower a bid once placed. Bids in the final minute extend the auction by another minute (anti-snipe).
- **Raffles** - enter for a chance at an experience.
No cash option here - everything is paid in MileagePlus miles.
how_to_access: You need a MileagePlus account; listings are filtered by member type - **General**, **Premier** (elite status), and **Cardmember**. Many of the best items are tagged Cardmember Exclusive or Premier Exclusive, meaning you must hold an eligible co-branded United card (the Chase United lineup - Explorer, Quest, Club Infinite, Gateway, and the United business cards) or hold Premier status to bid or buy. General-access items are open to any member.
standout_examples: Recent live listings show the range: a ten-course chef's-table dinner at Blue Duck Tavern in Washington, D.C. (auction, bidding into the 90,000-mile range); "Fly to New York to watch Wrexham AFC play Liverpool FC," a Premier Exclusive travel-plus-match package (auction, bids past 300,000 miles); Chicago White Sox Scout Seats and batting practice (from 15,000 miles); and a concert at San Francisco's Chase Center. Inventory rotates constantly and skews to United's hub cities (Chicago, New York, San Francisco, Washington D.C.), so the specific events change week to week.
good_to_know: Everything is non-refundable: miles are not returned once redeemed, and a no-show forfeits your miles with no reschedule - though you can usually send an eligible substitute if you contact MileagePlus in advance. Auctions are binding the moment you win. Inventory is heavily US-centric and concentrated in United hub markets, so options thin out if you're not near a major city. Browse and filter by member type, category, and location at exclusives.mileageplus.com, and sign up for SMS alerts so you don't miss a drop.
value_take: It's one of the few legit ways to turn United miles into access you genuinely can't buy off the shelf - chef's tables, premium sports seating, and airline-insider experiences. Treat it as access and flexibility rather than a redemption to maximize, and only bid miles you'd otherwise let sit, since it's all binding and non-refundable.

intro: Amex Experiences is American Express's entertainment-access platform - the place where your card gets you in the (virtual) door before the general public. It is less a points-redemption store and more a presale and reserved-ticket engine across live music, sports, theater, and dining, with a fancier Platinum/Centurion-only tier on top. Think of it as a perk that buys you timing and access, not necessarily a discount.
what_you_get:
- **Amex Presale Tickets and Reserved Tickets** - early access to buy seats for concerts, tours, sporting events, and theater before the general on-sale, plus blocks of seats Amex holds back for cardholders.
- **Music** - presales for major tours and festivals (Coachella has been a recurring marquee).
- **Sports** - access to events like the US Open Tennis Championships and major-market games.
- **Theater and arts** - Broadway and touring productions, preferred seating, and cardmember performances.
- **Dining and culinary** - celebrity-chef dinners, tastings, and cooking classes.
- **Premium Events Collection** - a Platinum/Centurion-only tier with VIP packages to headline events (think Coachella VIP, Grand Prix de Monaco access).
- **Venue benefits** - dedicated entrances, presale access, and (for enrolled US cardholders) 10% back on concessions at venues in the Amex Venue Collection.
how_it_works:
This is mostly **access, not a fixed points catalog**. You browse americanexpress.com/entertainment by artist, event, or city, hit "find tickets," and log in. Presales run for a set window before the public on-sale; Reserved Tickets are seat blocks Amex holds for cardholders.

- **Payment:** tickets must be charged to an eligible American Express card. On some events you may also see an option to pay with **Membership Rewards points at checkout** - but it is event-dependent, not universal.
- **Pricing:** prices and fees are set by the third-party ticket seller, promoter, or venue (often Ticketmaster) - Amex provides the access, not the price.
- **No auctions or bidding** here - it is straight presale/reserved purchase, not a bid-to-win model.

Note: the old "Events by Amex" branding was retired around June 10, 2026, but the access lives on at americanexpress.com/entertainment.
how_to_access: Open to **eligible American Express US Card Members** broadly - general cardholders get presale access, preferred seating, cardmember performances, and virtual experiences. The **Premium Events Collection** (the VIP-package tier) is reserved for **The Platinum Card, Business Platinum, and Centurion** holders. Concessions cash-back at Venue Collection sites requires enrollment. You access everything by logging in at americanexpress.com/entertainment with an eligible card.
standout_examples: Specific inventory rotates constantly, but recently featured access has included **Coachella** (with VIP packages via the Premium Events Collection), the **US Open Tennis Championships**, the **Grand Prix de Monaco**, major-market sports (Lakers, Clippers, Kings), and Broadway presales. Treat these as illustrative - what is live changes by season and city, so check the entertainment hub for current events.
good_to_know: Tickets are sold and fulfilled by third-party sellers (frequently Ticketmaster), so their rules govern - sales are typically **final / non-refundable**, with purchase limits, blackout dates, and limited supply. Inventory is **US-focused** and city-specific; presale windows are short, so timing matters. Paying with Membership Rewards points is offered on some events but not all - do not count on it. Find everything by logging in at americanexpress.com/entertainment and searching by artist, event, or city.
value_take: Worth knowing because the real prize is access and timing - getting a presale shot at a sold-out tour or a VIP package you literally cannot buy elsewhere. The points-or-cash flexibility on some events is a nice bonus, but treat this as a card perk, not a points-redemption play.

intro: Bilt Experiences is the "money can't buy" arm of Bilt Rewards - a rotating slate of member-only events you book with points, cash, or both. Think chef tasting menus at hot restaurants, comedy nights in unique venues, fitness pop-ups, and splashy Rent Day stunts (a recent one had Madonna hosting album-release parties in NY, LA, and Chicago). It is less a fixed catalog and more a steady drip of limited drops, with most of the marquee stuff tied to the 1st of each month (Rent Day).
what_you_get:
Bilt Experiences clusters into a few real categories:

- **Neighborhood Dining** - curated tasting menus from renowned chefs at participating restaurants, with member-exclusive pricing and premium cocktails. Bilt offers up to $600/year (roughly $50/month starting March 2026) in dining-experience credit.
- **Comedy & live entertainment** - standard comedy-club nights (drinks included) and pricier "bespoke" shows at unique venues with food and drink. Same up-to-$600/year structure as dining.
- **Music & celebrity events** - member-only release parties, performances, and one-off cultural moments (the Madonna Confessions II parties + exclusive vinyl drop are the recent headline).
- **Fitness pop-ups** - complimentary classes with names like SoulCycle and Barry's, usually surfacing on Rent Day.
- **Travel & access** - the booking side of Bilt is its 1:1 transfer partners and travel portal, but Experiences layers in the occasional "can't buy it anywhere else" perk.
how_it_works: Most experiences are **points-or-cash** at a fixed published price - for example a comedy night runs about $30-$40 or 2,000-2,500 Bilt Points, and a bespoke show runs about $75 or 5,000 points. You pick whichever you'd rather spend, and on some bookings you can mix in Bilt Cash (up to $50 toward one dining experience, rest in cash). This is fixed-price access, not an auction or bidding war - you reserve a slot while inventory lasts. The headline drops land on **Rent Day (the 1st of each month)**, so timing matters more than haggling.
how_to_access: Open to Bilt Rewards members (you pay rent through Bilt or use the Bilt Card). The catch is the booking window: higher elite tiers get in first. Bilt has four tiers - Blue, Silver, Gold, Platinum - earned by qualifying points or eligible spend (Silver ~50K pts or $10K spend; Gold ~125K pts or $25K; Platinum ~200K pts or $50K). Platinum gets first priority on Rent Day bookings, then Gold, ahead of Silver and Blue. So everyone can play, but for the scarce, sell-out experiences your status decides whether there's anything left when your window opens.
standout_examples:
Recent, real examples (inventory rotates monthly, so treat these as a flavor, not a standing menu):

- **Madonna "Confessions II" release parties** (June 2026 Rent Day) - member-only events in New York, LA, and Chicago on the July 3 album-drop date, with cocktails, passed appetizers, and a DJ, for $40 or 2,500 points per person, plus a Bilt-exclusive limited-edition vinyl with custom artwork.
- **Neighborhood chef dinners** - curated tasting menus at 30 restaurants across five cities on a single Rent Day, at member-exclusive pricing.
- **Comedy nights** - club shows (~$30-$40 or 2,000-2,500 points) and premium "bespoke" sets at unique venues (~$75 or 5,000 points), drinks/bites included.
- **Fitness pop-ups** - complimentary SoulCycle and Barry's classes tied to Rent Day.
good_to_know: Inventory is regional and limited - the best experiences run in a handful of major cities (NY, LA, Chicago and similar) and sell out, so you may see nothing in your area some months. Find offers in the Bilt app, especially around Rent Day (the 1st). Bilt Cash has strings: only $100 rolls over year to year and the rest expires at calendar year-end, so plan to use it. The dining and comedy credits cap at roughly $50/month and up to $600/year each. Refund and change terms vary by event - read the specific listing before you commit.
value_take: Worth knowing for the points-or-cash flexibility and genuine access - chef tastings, comedy in cool rooms, and the occasional celebrity moment you can't book elsewhere. Just don't expect a deep year-round catalog: this is a limited, Rent-Day-driven drip where your elite tier and your city decide how much you actually get.

intro: Capital One Entertainment is the bank's ticketing-and-experiences platform, where eligible cardholders can grab tickets to concerts, sports, theater and dining events - and pay with Capital One rewards, their card, or a mix of both. Beyond the everyday 500,000-plus events powered by Vivid Seats, the real draw is the cardholder-exclusive stuff: presale access, VIP packages, athlete meet-and-greets, and chef dinners you cannot just walk up and buy. Think of it as flexibility plus a velvet-rope line, not a points-maximizing play.
what_you_get:
- **Music** - concert tickets, premium seats, exclusive sound checks, and artist meet-and-greets (including iHeartRadio festival and event access)
- **Sports** - tickets and VIP packages; as the official bank partner of the NCAA and MLB, marquee access like the World Series, College Football National Championship, and the Capital One Orange Bowl
- **Dining** - cardholder-only dinners with Michelin-starred and James Beard chefs, plus access at top food festivals
- **Theater** - presale access to Broadway performances
- **Money-can't-buy VIP** - occasional premium packages (private orchestra receptions, curated golf trips, etc.) that rotate in and out
how_it_works:
Most inventory is **fixed-price** and powered by Vivid Seats - you pick the event, choose seats, and check out. You can pay three ways: **redeem rewards, charge your eligible Capital One card, or split it** between rewards and card. Not every event supports every payment method - the available options show up at checkout, and for split payments you toggle how many miles or how much cash-back you want to apply.

Separately, **cardholder-exclusive presales** (at capitalone.com/pre-sales) are an access perk, not a redemption - they get you early buying windows before the general public, but those presale tickets are bought on the regular ticket seller's site, not on the Entertainment platform itself.
how_to_access: The Entertainment ticketing platform is open to anyone with a **US-issued, Capital One (or Discover by Capital One) branded rewards consumer or small-business credit card** in good standing, age 18+. Debit cards, private-label retail cards, and co-brand partner cards are NOT eligible for the platform. No specific premium tier is required, but earn rates differ: **Savor** earns 8% cash back on Entertainment purchases, and **Venture X, Venture X Business, Venture, Venture Business, and Spark 2X miles** cards earn 5X miles. Access it via the Capital One app, capitalone.com, or entertainment.capitalone.com. (The separate cardholder presales are open more broadly - including eligible debit and co-brand cards.)
standout_examples: Recently featured cardholder access has included the **MLB World Series presented by Capital One**, the **College Football National Championship** and **Capital One Orange Bowl**, **iHeartRadio Music Festival** seats and artist sound checks, **James Beard Foundation and Michelin Guide culinary events**, and Broadway presales. Premium one-off packages have included a private reception and performance with the New York Philharmonic and a golf trip across iconic English links courses. Inventory rotates constantly and varies by region and availability, so the exact lineup changes throughout the year.
good_to_know: All orders are **final - non-refundable and non-cancelable** once placed, except when the event provider cancels (then you're refunded to original payment, with split rewards/card orders refunded proportionally). Cardholder-exclusive tickets cannot be resold; other Vivid Seats tickets may be transferred or resold. Postponed events are NOT refunded. Vivid Seats prices are set by independent resellers and can run above or below face value. Exclusive tickets are limited and first-come, first-served, with per-order limits. Browse inventory in the Capital One app or at entertainment.capitalone.com; find presales at capitalone.com/pre-sales.
value_take: Worth knowing for the cardholder-exclusive access - presales, VIP packages, and chef dinners you cannot get elsewhere - and for the genuine convenience of paying with rewards, card, or both. For ordinary tickets, redeeming rewards here is straightforward and flexible, though enthusiasts often get more mileage from Capital One's transfer partners; just remember every purchase is binding.

intro: Chase Experiences is Chase's events platform that turns your card (and your Ultimate Rewards points) into a backstage pass - presale tickets, premium seats, VIP hospitality, and curated trips you can't just buy off Ticketmaster. The headline acts are concerts, sports, and festivals open to most Chase cardholders, with a whole upper tier of money-can't-buy stuff reserved for Sapphire cardholders. Think of it as the perks layer that sits next to Chase Travel, not a separate currency.
what_you_get:
Categories that actually show up:

- **Concerts and music festivals** - presale access, cardholder-only seating, and discounts at venues and events like Lollapalooza.
- **Sports** - early ticket offers, preferred seating, and upgrades at sponsored venues like Madison Square Garden, the Chase Center, and the US Open.
- **Chase Lounges** - elevated food-and-beverage lounges at partner venues (e.g. Madison Square Garden, the Chicago Theatre) for eligible cardholders.
- **Dining (Sapphire)** - ticketed dinners and immersive pop-ups via the Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables collection on OpenTable.
- **Curated travel (Sapphire Reserve)** - once-in-a-lifetime Sapphire Reserve Trips designed by Chase Travel around cultural moments and marquee destinations.
- **Entertainment tie-ins (Sapphire Reserve)** - exclusive first-look content and pop-ups tied to Apple TV and Apple Music.
how_it_works:
Mostly **access plus points-or-cash**, not an auction:

- You browse what's live, then **pay with your eligible Chase card or redeem Ultimate Rewards points** to book. Points redeem at a flat 1 cent per point against the ticket cost - no bidding, no derived gymnastics.
- A lot of the value is **access itself**: presale windows, cardholder seating blocks, lounge entry, and upgrades you unlock by paying with the card - no points required.
- For ticketed concerts and sports, you often go through partners like Ticketmaster and filter for the Chase presale, then check out with your Chase card.
how_to_access: Generally **open to all Chase credit cardholders** - sign in through the Chase Experiences portal (chase.com/personal/events/experiences) to see what's live in your area, then pay with an eligible Chase card or Ultimate Rewards points. The premium tier is **card-gated**: Chase Sapphire Preferred and Sapphire Reserve cardholders unlock private dinners and VIP concert/sports access, and the richest stuff - Exclusive Tables, Sapphire Reserve Trips, and the Apple content experiences - is reserved for **Sapphire Reserve and Sapphire Reserve for Business** cardmembers.
standout_examples: Inventory rotates, but recent and confirmed-for-2026 examples give the flavor: premium-access concerts at Madison Square Garden, US Open and Lollapalooza activations, and the 2026 Sapphire Reserve Trips lineup - skiing and snowboarding in St. Moritz (February), Holi the Festival of Colors in Jaipur (March), an oceanfront wellness retreat in Turks and Caicos (May), Formula E with Jaguar TCS Racing in London (August), and Surf Ranch with the World Surf League in Lemoore, California (October). On the dining side, Sapphire Reserve Exclusive Tables surfaces primetime reservations at award-winning restaurants across cities like NYC, Chicago, LA, and San Francisco.
good_to_know: Find inventory by signing into the Chase Experiences portal or filtering for the Chase presale on partners like Ticketmaster. Availability is heavily **regional and event-driven** - what's live depends on your market and the calendar, and Sapphire Reserve Trips have limited spots that sell out. Points always redeem at 1 cent each here, so this is a cost-offset, not a transfer-to-airline play. intro: Citi Entertainment is the bank's cardholder perk that unlocks presales, preferred seats, VIP upgrades, and the occasional comp ticket to thousands of live events every year - concerts, games, comedy, dining, family shows. Think of it less as a points store and more as a velvet rope: if you carry an eligible Citi card or debit card, you get in line before the general public.
what_you_get:
Access to four kinds of offers across a rotating live-events calendar:

- **Presales** - buy tickets during a limited window (usually 2-3 days) before they go on sale to everyone else
- **Preferred Tickets** - a Citi-only allotment held back for cardholders for a limited time
- **VIP Packages** - premium seating plus extras like artist merch, meet-and-greets, and hospitality access
- **Complimentary Tickets** - occasional free tickets to select events

Categories span concerts (every genre), sports, comedy and magic, dining with top chefs, and family shows.
how_it_works:
This is **access, not redemption** - you pay cash for the tickets at face/preferred pricing, you do not spend points. Citi Entertainment is essentially a discovery hub: browse events on the site, then get routed to a ticketing partner (usually Ticketmaster) to actually buy.

To unlock a presale you either (1) enter the first six digits of your eligible Citi card number at checkout, or (2) link your Citi card account to your Ticketmaster account once for the year.

Note on ThankYou points: you cannot apply them at the Citi Entertainment / Ticketmaster checkout. You can only redeem points as a 1-cent-per-point statement credit after the charge posts.
how_to_access: Open to all Citi credit card and Citibank debit card customers - no specific premium card or elite tier required. Unlock by entering your card's first six digits at the partner checkout, or by linking your Citi card account to Ticketmaster (re-link at least once a year to keep access to future presales).
standout_examples: Inventory rotates constantly, but recently featured offers have included presale access to major touring artists (Sting, Shania Twain, Jelly Roll, Rush's Fifty Something Tour), comedy from Chelsea Handler, the Harlem Globetrotters and select college football, Kidz Bop Live for families, and culinary nights like the No Kid Hungry chef dinners. The exact lineup changes weekly, so treat these as the flavor rather than a fixed menu.
good_to_know:
- You pay full ticket price - this is early/exclusive access, not a discount program (though VIP packages bundle in extras).
- Presale windows are short (often 2-3 days) and inventory is limited, so move fast.
- Purchases happen on the partner site (Ticketmaster), and refundability follows that partner's and the event's policy - all-sales-final is common for live events.
- Offers are tied to specific events and markets, so availability is regional and event-driven.
- Re-link your card to Ticketmaster at least once a year or you'll lose presale access.
- Find inventory at citientertainment.com, browsable by category and location.
value_take: Worth knowing because it's a free perk on nearly every Citi card - the value is in beating the general public to seats for in-demand tours and snagging VIP extras you can't otherwise buy. Just don't expect to pay with points; this is an access play, not a redemption one.

intro: Virgin Red is Virgin's free rewards club - a UK-and-US lifestyle catalog where Virgin Points you earn (or transfer in) get spent on Virgin and partner-brand treats. Think gift cards and spa days at the small end, full Virgin Voyages cruises and Virgin Hotels nights at the big end. The headline perk: Virgin Points never expire, and the same currency books Virgin Atlantic award flights once you link your Flying Club account.
what_you_get:
Virgin Red carries 200+ rewards across a wide spread of categories:

- **Gift cards and everyday treats** - digital gift cards (e.g. Starbucks) and retailer vouchers at low point counts.
- **Wellness and fitness** - boutique class credits (Barry's), spa days, Virgin Active access.
- **Experiences and days out** - family attractions, dining, afternoon tea, and bucket-list activities (catalog rotates).
- **Travel** - Virgin Hotels stays, Virgin Atlantic Holidays packages, and Virgin Voyages cruises (cabin upgrades, partial or full sailings).
- **Wine and merchandise** - Virgin Wines cases and branded goods.
- **Award flights** - link Virgin Atlantic Flying Club and the same points book flights and upgrades.
how_it_works:
It's a **fixed-price catalog**, not an auction. You browse "Spend," pick a reward, and redeem at the published Virgin Points price - small stuff starts in the low thousands of points, while cruises and hotel nights run into the tens or hundreds of thousands.

A few mechanics worth knowing:
- Points and cash don't mix on a single catalog item - you redeem with points, full stop (Virgin Atlantic Holidays packages are the exception, where points can cover part or all of a booking).
- Virgin Points are a transferable currency: you can move them in from partners and link Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, Virgin Hotels The Know, and Virgin Wines Discovery so all your points show as one balance.
- Points **never expire**, so you can stockpile toward a bigger reward.
how_to_access: Open to everyone 18+ who is a **UK or US resident** - you do not need to already be a Virgin customer. Joining is free via the website or app. No card or elite tier is required to redeem. If you do hold Virgin Atlantic Flying Club, Virgin Hotels The Know, or Virgin Wines Discovery, you can link those accounts to pool points. The co-brand **Virgin Red Rewards Mastercard** (Synchrony, $99 annual fee) is a way to earn faster but is not required for access.
standout_examples: Specific catalog items rotate, but recent US examples give the range: a $10 Starbucks digital gift card from around 2,000 points at the low end; a Barry's class credit from about 3,500 points; Virgin Hotels nights from roughly 60,000 points; and a Central Sea Terrace cabin on a Virgin Voyages cruise from about 250,000 points. Spa days and experience-style rewards typically land in the mid-thousands to ~15,000 points. Treat any single item as a snapshot - inventory and pricing shift.
good_to_know: Browse live inventory under "Spend" on virgin.com/virgin-red or the app; favorite items with the heart icon to track toward a balance. Eligibility is geo-gated to UK and US residents, and the US catalog differs from the UK one (UK-only items like Virgin Trains tickets won't apply to US members). Vouchers you buy sit in "My rewards"; physical goods (wine, merch, tickets) show under "Orders." Redemptions are generally final - check each reward's terms for any refund or change rules before you commit, since catalog redemptions usually aren't reversible. Points never expire.
value_take: Worth knowing because it's a flexible, never-expiring currency that does double duty: low-effort lifestyle treats on one end, and high-value Virgin Atlantic award flights and Virgin Voyages sailings on the other once you link Flying Club. The points-or-flights optionality is the real draw.
refundable: Varies by reward (catalog redemptions usually final)

intro: Priceless is Mastercard's experiences and access platform - the place where your plain plastic suddenly unlocks concert presales, chef's-table dinners, museum-after-dark tours, and one-of-a-kind events you cannot just buy on Ticketmaster. It is not a points program in the airline-mile sense; it is a benefits hub where the value is the access itself, with payment handled on your Mastercard. Think of it as the velvet rope your card has been holding the whole time.
what_you_get:
Priceless organizes curated experiences into a handful of recurring categories:

- **Music and concerts** - presale and preferred ticket access via the Mastercard x Live Nation partnership, plus premium seats and VIP packages
- **Culinary** - chef's-table dinners, tastings, and dining events with notable restaurants and chefs
- **Sports** - access to marquee matches, tournaments, and behind-the-scenes sporting moments
- **Arts and theater** - curator-led museum tours, opera with cast meet-and-greets, and stage performances
- **Travel and lifestyle** - destination experiences, hidden-gem local activities, and luxury escapes

Mastercard markets 1,000+ experiences globally, and the lineup rotates constantly.
how_it_works:
There is no single mechanic - Priceless blends a few:

- **Cardholder presale / preferred tickets (access)** - the headline use case. Eligible cardholders get early or reserved access to concert and event tickets before the general public, then pay with their Mastercard. Presale windows are typically up to 48 hours ahead of public on-sale.
- **Fixed-price experiences** - many curated experiences are listed at a set price and booked directly (checkout, email-to-book, call-to-book, or voucher download).
- **Auction / bid experiences** - some exclusive, money-can't-buy items run as auctions where you bid against other cardholders; the highest bid at the close wins.

Across all of it, payment runs on your Mastercard - this is a card-access platform, not a points-redemption marketplace.
how_to_access: Browsing priceless.com is open to anyone, but redeeming usually requires registering and paying with an eligible Mastercard. Mastercard runs four consumer tiers - standard Mastercard, World, World Elite, and World Legend - and the better perks gate upward. The Preferred Tickets benefit (reserved inventory held back from general sale) is specifically for World Elite and World Legend consumer credit cardholders, while general presale access via the Live Nation partnership is open to most consumer Mastercard credit cardholders. Anything involving payment must be charged to a Mastercard.
standout_examples: Inventory rotates often, so specific listings come and go - but the anchor is the multi-year Mastercard x Live Nation partnership, which gives 100M+ cardholders presale and premium-seat access to major tours and festivals worldwide. Beyond music, recurring standouts include culinary events (chef's-table dinners and tastings), curator-led museum and arts experiences, and access to marquee sporting events. The most exclusive items - true money-can't-buy moments - often surface as cardholder auctions. Check priceless.com for what is live in your market right now.
good_to_know: Inventory is heavily regional - what is live in the US differs from the UK, EU, or Asia, and the Live Nation benefit rolled out across roughly 19 geographies. Tiered perks (Preferred Tickets) require a World Elite or World Legend card, and all paid bookings must run on a Mastercard. Auctions are binding once you win - bid like you mean it. Refundability varies entirely by experience and partner, so read the terms on each listing before you commit. Find everything by browsing priceless.com and filtering by city/category, or by watching for presale codes during a card-linked on-sale.
value_take: Worth knowing because it is a benefit you already have - early access to concerts and curated experiences that can be genuinely hard to get any other way. The flexibility (presale, fixed-price, and auction options) means there is usually a way in, even if it is access rather than points value.

intro: Visa Signature and Visa Infinite Experiences is not a points marketplace - it's Visa's access engine, baked into the card you already carry. Instead of redeeming points, you get presale windows, free tickets, and curated dining and concert nights that the general public can't touch. Think of it as the velvet rope your card swings open, no separate signup or membership fee required.
what_you_get:
- **Live music** - intimate concerts and film-set performances (the Sofar Sounds tie-in), plus 7-day presale windows and one free ticket per show for Signature/Infinite holders
- **Culinary** - the Visa Infinite Dining Series: coursed meals with paired cocktails, hands-on cooking classes, and personal-chef nights with named chefs
- **Sports** - early access to apply for marquee events (e.g. the FIFA World Cup 26 Visa Presale Draw)
- **Concierge** - 24/7 Visa Infinite concierge to chase down tickets, reservations, and event access
- Content perks like director's-cut concert films and behind-the-scenes footage
how_it_works:
This runs on **access, not redemption**. There's no "spend 25,000 points" cart. Instead:
- **Presale windows** - eligible cardholders get an exclusive advance window (often 7 days) before tickets open to the public.
- **Presale draws** - for high-demand events (like the FIFA World Cup), you apply during an entry period and a random draw selects who gets to buy.
- **Free/included tickets** - Signature and Infinite holders get one free Sofar Sounds ticket per show with purchase of one or more; standard booking fees are waived on the free ticket.
- **Curated events** - dining-series seats are booked directly through Visa's event listings; pay the event price, no points involved.
You pay cash for the actual ticket or meal - the card is your access key, not your wallet of points.
how_to_access: Gated by card tier, not an opt-in membership. Visa Infinite and Visa Infinite Privilege cardholders get the deepest access, including the Dining Series and Infinite Experiences. Visa Signature cardholders get consumer-tier perks like the Sofar Sounds presale window and one free ticket per show. Some sports presales (notably the FIFA World Cup 26 draw) open to all Visa cardholders - credit, debit, or reloadable prepaid - so the floor varies by event. No separate fee or signup; eligibility rides on whatever Visa product your issuer gave you, and specific perks also depend on whether your issuer chose to include them.
standout_examples:
- **FIFA World Cup 26 Visa Presale Draw** - Visa cardholders worldwide got first crack at applying for 2026 tournament tickets via a randomized draw, ahead of general sale (group-stage tickets started at $60).
- **Visa Infinite Dining Series** - in 2024, Infinite cardholders cooked alongside Chef Brandon Jew of Mister Jiu's in San Francisco for a hands-on open-fire class followed by a four-course Asian-cuisine menu.
- **Sofar Sounds concerts** - intimate shows (often capped around 250 attendees) on closed sets, with a 7-day cardholder presale and one free ticket per show.
Inventory rotates by city and season - exact lineups change constantly.
good_to_know:
- It's an **access benefit, not a points program** - don't expect a redemption catalog or fixed point prices.
- **Presale draws are a lottery** - entering doesn't guarantee tickets; selection is random and you still pay for the seats you win.
- **Heavily US/North-America weighted** for the dining and concert series; availability is city-by-city and rotates, so check what's live near you.
- **Refundability follows the event/venue policy**, not Visa - read the fine print before you buy.
- Find inventory through Visa's experiences pages, partner sites (Sofar Sounds), event-specific microsites, and the 24/7 Visa Infinite concierge line.
value_take: Worth knowing because it's free access you already hold - presale windows, waived fees, and chef-led nights you can't buy your way into otherwise. Just treat it as a door-opener, not a points-earning play, and go in clear-eyed that high-demand events run on a draw.

intro: Limitless Experiences by ALL is Accor's redemption playground beyond hotel nights - the place where your Reward points buy access to concerts, sports, travel adventures, and genuine money-can't-buy moments. Think pitchside at a Paris Saint-Germain match, suite tickets to a headliner show at Accor Arena, or a hot-air balloon over Tuscany. Accor advertises 2,000+ experiences across 65+ cities, heavily weighted toward Europe and Asia-Pacific where its brands run deep.
what_you_get:
Reward points unlock a rotating catalog of access-driven experiences, not just stays:
- **Sports** - VIP and reserved seats at partner venues like Parc des Princes (PSG matches) and Accor Stadium in Sydney
- **Entertainment and concerts** - tickets and suites to shows at Accor Arena Paris and other partner venues
- **Travel and adventure** - hot-air balloon flights, VIP sailing trips, guided and curated escapes
- **Money-can't-buy moments** - meet-and-greets, signed merchandise, behind-the-scenes access tied to Accor's sponsorships
- **Auctions and prize draws** - bid points on, or buy raffle tickets for, one-off experiences and memorabilia
- **Lifestyle and retail** - through the shopping portal you can also grab car rentals, train tickets, electronics, luggage, and wine, or convert points to airline miles
how_it_works:
There are a few different mechanics depending on the item:
- **Fixed point price** - many catalog experiences have a set Reward-points cost (redemptions generally move in blocks tied to Accor's standard 2,000 points = 40 EUR conversion).
- **Auctions** - you bid your Reward points against other members; highest bid wins, and bids are binding.
- **Prize draws / raffles** - you buy entry tickets with points (commonly 500 or 1,000 Reward points per ticket) for a chance to win; you are paying for a chance, not the item.
- **Cash or points** - some retail and travel items on the shopping portal can be paid with points, cash, or a mix.
Inventory rotates constantly and is regional, so what you see depends on your market.
how_to_access: Open to all ALL - Accor Live Limitless members at no extra cost - you just need a points balance (minimum 1,000 points / 20 EUR to begin redeeming, then in 2,000-point blocks). No specific credit card or elite tier is required to browse or redeem, though premium experiences and certain auctions are priced high enough that they effectively favor heavy earners and elite members. Access the catalog through the Limitless Experiences hub (limitlessexperiences.accor.com) signed in to your ALL account; availability is gated by region.
standout_examples: Recurring marquee inventory includes Paris Saint-Germain matchday access at Parc des Princes (reserved seats, VIP, pitchside, plus PSG prize draws for tickets, signed jerseys, and player meet-and-greets), concerts and shows at Accor Arena in Paris, and VIP seating and family entertainment at Accor Stadium in Sydney. Travel-side highlights have featured hot-air balloon flights over Tuscany and VIP sailing trips. Specific experiences rotate frequently and vary by region, so treat these as the categories to watch rather than a fixed menu.
good_to_know: Auctions are binding - if you win, those points are gone, so bid like you mean it. Prize-draw tickets buy a chance, not the prize. Inventory is strongly regional (Europe and Asia-Pacific dominate; US-based members will find slimmer pickings) and rotates often, so check the Limitless Experiences hub regularly. Standard Accor redemption rules apply (1,000-point minimum, 2,000-point blocks), and experience-specific terms, blackout dates, and refundability are set per listing - read each one. Some shopping-portal items also bill in cash or points-plus-cash.
value_take: It's a legitimately strong way to turn hotel points into access you can't easily buy - especially PSG, Accor Arena, and Accor Stadium events tied to Accor's sponsorships. Just go in clear-eyed about the regional skew and the binding auction format.

intro: Choice Privileges Experiences is the hotel program's auction house for bucket-list moments - think NASCAR pit access, college football VIP tickets, and concerts - that you bid on with points instead of booking outright. It runs at experiencesbychoice.com, and the twist is that you are competing against other members rather than paying a fixed price. Open to any Choice Privileges member for free, it turns a humble roadside-hotel currency into front-row access.
what_you_get:
Rotating experiences across a handful of categories:
- **Motorsports / NASCAR** - VIP raceday packages (think Trackhouse Racing tie-ins, pit and garage tours, pre-race food and beverage, driver and pit-crew meet-and-greets) at tracks like Daytona, Atlanta, and Winston-Salem.
- **College sports** - VIP game-day access, often the fastest to sell out.
- **Concerts / music** - tiered packages (for example Kane Brown shows in Silver, Gold, and Platinum levels).
- **Pro sports and entertainment** - NHL games, Topgolf outings, and similar.

Inventory is finite per event and rotates, so the exact lineup changes throughout the year.
how_it_works:
This is an **auction**, not a fixed-price redemption. You browse live experiences at experiencesbychoice.com, then place a points bid (or hit "Watch" to follow it). Bids start around **10,000 points** for many experiences, though marquee NASCAR Cup packages have opened higher (around 40,000 points), and winning bids run well above the floor since you are competing against other members.

You can raise your bid as many times as you like before the auction closes, and you get an email each time. When the auction ends you are notified whether you won. The key mechanic on points: **if you win, your points are spent and not refunded; if you lose, your bid points are returned to your account.** So your points are only ever at risk on a winning bid - but a winning bid is binding.
how_to_access: Open to any **Choice Privileges** member, and membership is free to join - no specific elite tier or co-brand card required to bid. You can view experiences and current bids without logging in, but you must sign in to your Choice Privileges account to place a bid. There is no published status gate, so a brand-new member with enough points can compete head-to-head with a Diamond. Holding the Choice Privileges Mastercard simply helps you earn points faster; it is not a requirement for access.
standout_examples: Recent and representative drops include VIP NASCAR raceday packages (Trackhouse Racing experiences, with tracks such as Daytona, Atlanta, and Winston-Salem on the 2026 calendar), tiered Kane Brown concert packages (Silver / Gold / Platinum), NHL game experiences, and Topgolf outings - alongside college-sports VIP access that tends to sell out fast. The specific lineup rotates, so treat these as the categories to expect rather than a fixed menu.
good_to_know: Find live inventory at experiencesbychoice.com (also linked from the Choice Privileges "redeem points" pages). Refund rule is the headline catch: points on a **winning** bid are gone and the experience itself is not refundable, while points on a **losing** bid are returned to you. Experiences are US-centric and event-driven, with limited slots per event - college-sports and high-demand drops can close within a day. You can keep raising your bid until the auction ends, so set a ceiling before you start. Travel, lodging, and incidentals are generally on you unless an experience states otherwise.
value_take: Worth knowing because it converts an everyday roadside-hotel currency into genuine money-can't-easily-buy access - pit lanes, end zones, and concert pits - with no status or card gate. Just go in with a firm bid ceiling, since a winning bid is binding and those points don't come back.
refundable: Losing bids refunded; winning bids are binding (no refund)
