intro: Hilton Honors Experiences is Hilton's redemption marketplace where members spend points (not just nights) on access-style outings - think sold-out concerts, sporting events, chef dinners, and spa or mixology packages. Some items have a fixed point price you just buy outright; most are bid-style Dutch auctions where the highest bidders win. It is the kind of corner most people forget exists, but it is one of the few ways to turn a point balance into actual access.
what_you_get:
Hilton partners with artists, teams, restaurants, and local providers to offer experiences across a handful of rotating categories:

- **Concerts and music** - intimate acoustic sessions, festival access, and up-close performances with featured artists
- **Sporting events** - tickets and VIP access to games, often otherwise hard to get
- **Culinary** - chef dinners, tastings, brunches, and dining curations
- **Wellness and activities** - spa packages, massages, mixology and cooking classes
- **Travel and cultural outings** - road-trip style "America Experiences" and local cultural trips, sometimes for as little as 250 points

Inventory rotates constantly, so the exact lineup changes by season and region.
how_it_works:
Two redemption mechanics, both paid entirely in Hilton Honors points:

- **Fixed-price (Buy Now)** - any experience with a Redeem button is offered at a set point amount in limited quantity, first come first served.
- **Auction (Bid)** - most marquee items run as a Dutch auction. Hilton sets an opening bid and a number of items; you bid at or above that minimum. At close, the highest bidders all win and pay the same price - the lowest successful bid. Ties break by quantity bid, then time placed.

You must hold enough points in your account to cover a bid at the time you place it (you can buy points to top off). Winning bids are debited automatically at auction close. Members can redeem up to five experiences per calendar year.
how_to_access: Open to all Hilton Honors members - no elite tier or specific co-brand card required. You just need a point balance large enough to cover the fixed price or your bid. Access the platform directly at experiences.hiltonhonors.com and sign in with your Honors account.
standout_examples: Inventory rotates, so the live lineup shifts week to week, but recent and recurring examples give the flavor: low-cost "America Experiences" road-trip outings redeemable for as little as 250 points, intimate acoustic concert sessions with featured artists, hard-to-get tickets to major sporting events, chef-led dinners and tastings, and spa, massage, and mixology-class packages. Marquee artist and sports items typically run as auctions and can cost tens or hundreds of thousands of points, while activities and culinary outings often sit at the lower fixed-price end.
good_to_know: All Experiences redemptions are final - they cannot be exchanged, modified, cancelled, or refunded, so an auction bid is binding the moment you win. You are capped at five experiences per calendar year. Availability is regional and the lineup rotates, so browse the live platform rather than assuming a past deal is still up. For auctions, make sure your point balance covers your bid before you place it, since points are debited automatically at close.
value_take: Worth knowing because it is one of the only loyalty platforms that turns points into genuine access - concerts, games, and chef tables you could not otherwise buy - with no status or card gating. Value swings widely by item and auction price, so treat it as an access play rather than a guaranteed deal.

intro: IHG One Rewards Access is the hotel chain's experiences platform - a place to spend your IHG points on things that aren't a hotel night: concerts, sporting events, chef's tables, and bucket-list trips. Some packages have a fixed points price you can grab instantly, others run as points auctions where the highest bidder wins. Think of it as a second life for the points you've been hoarding, if you'd rather have a memory than a free room.
what_you_get:
Rotating experience packages across a handful of categories:
- Entertainment - concerts, music, and exclusive performances
- Sports - tickets and on-site access to live events
- Culinary - cooking classes, chef's tables, and high-end dining reservations
- Culture and arts - theater, dance, and cultural events
- Travel and getaways - curated trips and stays bundled with experiences
- Money-can't-buy and VIP access - private performances, behind-the-scenes, and meet-and-greet style packages
Inventory rotates constantly, and packages are region-specific, so what's live depends on when and where you're looking.
how_it_works:
Two redemption mechanics, both paid entirely in IHG points (not cash):
- **Redeem Now** - a fixed points price you pay to claim the package instantly while it's available.
- **Bid Now** - a points auction on a single package; the highest bid at the close of the auction period wins. Each package is its own auction, and some rewards have multiple packages (so multiple winners).
Points are debited automatically when you win or redeem, and you can track everything on the Bid Status page. After you secure an experience, the IHG One Rewards Access team reaches out within about 3-5 business days to confirm the details. There's no cap on how many rewards you can win or buy, but you need enough points in your account to cover every active bid at once.
how_to_access: Open to any IHG One Rewards member with a valid account who is 18 or older - no elite status or co-brand card required to participate. That said, some premium packages are gated: select prizes are reserved for higher tiers (such as Platinum Elite or Diamond Elite), and some require you to be 21+. You spend regular IHG One Rewards points, so the easiest way to stock up is the usual routes - paid stays, the IHG One Rewards Premier or Traveler cards, and transfers from partners like Chase into IHG.
standout_examples: Examples rotate, but recently featured packages have included a private performance by Lily Fitts paired with a cocktail workshop led by beverage specialist Belinda Chang; drinks and light bites at the InterContinental Boston followed by a sunset Boston Harbor dinner cruise; and tickets to Bangarra Dance Theatre's national tour in Australia. The mix skews toward live entertainment, culinary events, and once-in-a-lifetime access rather than everyday gift cards.
good_to_know: Big catch: all sales are final. No refunds on winning bids or Redeem Now redemptions, and rewards can't be exchanged, modified, cancelled, or refunded once secured - a bid is binding, so don't place one you're not ready to honor. Inventory is regional and time-limited, so availability varies by country and rotates fast; browse current packages at auctions.ihg.com (the IHG One Rewards Access site). Some packages carry tier or age restrictions, and you must hold enough points to cover all your active bids simultaneously.
value_take: Worth knowing because it's a flexible exit for points you might otherwise let sit, and the access angle - private performances, chef's tables, money-can't-buy events - can be genuinely hard to buy any other way. Just treat bids as final and go in with a specific experience you actually want, not as a way to "use up" a balance.

intro: Marriott Bonvoy Moments is the brand's experiences marketplace - the place to spend Bonvoy points (or sometimes cash) on things you can't just book, like VIP concert access, courtside seats, chef's-table dinners, and once-in-a-lifetime sporting events. Some packages are sold at a fixed price, others go to the highest bidder in a points auction, and a handful drop for as little as 1 point if you're fast. Open to any Bonvoy member, with a steady stream of new inventory tied to whatever's on the global events calendar.
what_you_get:
The catalog is organized into four core categories:

- **Culinary** - chef's-table dinners, tastings, festivals, and epicurean experiences (e.g. sake tastings, VIP food festival access with meet-and-greets).
- **Arts & Lifestyle** - premieres, galas, cultural excursions, and exclusive lifestyle events.
- **Sports** - VIP access, hospitality packages, and athlete meet-and-greets at major events (FIFA World Cup 2026, ICC Women's T20 World Cup, motorsport at Silverstone/Spielberg).
- **Entertainment** - concerts, music festivals, and private performances, often bundled with hotel stays.

Many packages bundle the experience with multi-night stays at Marriott properties. There's also a separate MGM Collection of entertainment and sporting Moments.
how_it_works:
Three redemption mechanics run side by side:

- **Fixed price** - a set number of points (or in some markets points-or-cash), deducted instantly, first-come first-served while packages last.
- **Auction** - highest bid at close wins. Bids are in 2,500-point increments; you can place a single one-time bid or set a max and let it auto-bid. Auctions typically run 15-30 days. **All bids are binding** - you can't lower or cancel.
- **1-Point Drops** - select Moments released for just 1 point, first-come first-served, very limited quantity. One 1-Point package per member per calendar year.

You can redeem up to two packages for the same Moment. All redemptions are final.
how_to_access: Open to any Marriott Bonvoy member - no elite status or specific co-brand card required. You just sign in with your Bonvoy account to bid or buy, and you need at least 1 point in your account before a 1-Point Drop redemption. Some individual Moments are gated to specific cardholders or regions (the scrape shows an "Amex Card Member Exclusive for Japan Cardholders Only" listing, and FIFA World Cup 2026 access is presented "thanks to Visa"), but the platform overall is membership-wide.
standout_examples: Inventory rotates constantly, but recent live and upcoming listings show the range: VIP access to All Points East festival in London via a 1-Point Drop; Celine Dion premium hospitality tickets in Paris paired with Renaissance hotel stays (auction); a sake tasting with Kuheiji Kuno plus a Kobe beef dinner at The Ritz-Carlton, Osaka; hospitality tickets to the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 final at Lord's; and a private Amber Mark concert with rooftop cocktails and a meet-and-greet at Moxy Lower East Side. Marriott is also offering access to all 104 FIFA World Cup 2026 matches.
good_to_know: Everything is final - no refunds, no cancellations, and Moments are not transferable (reselling can forfeit both the experience and your points). Auction bids are binding the moment you place them. Inventory is geographically clustered (lots of US, UK, Europe, and Asia listings; you search by city or keyword), so the best Moments aren't always near you, and travel/stays are sometimes but not always bundled in. You can buy Bonvoy points to top up for a redemption. Browse by category or use the location search on the Moments site to find what's currently live, plus "Coming Soon" and "Ending Soon" rails.
value_take: Worth knowing because it's genuine money-can't-buy access - VIP festival entry, World Cup matches, private concerts - that you literally cannot book any other way, and the points-or-cash flexibility plus 1-point drops make it an easy way to use a Bonvoy balance on an experience instead of a room night. Just go in clear-eyed: bids and buys are binding, so only commit to a Moment you'd actually travel for.
refundable: No - all redemptions and bids are final and non-transferable

intro: FIND is World of Hyatt's curated experiences platform - think truffle hunting, chef-led cooking sessions, jungle safaris, and horseback rides you can book with points or cash. It is built around wellbeing rather than concerts and stadiums, and you do not need to be staying at a Hyatt to book one.
what_you_get:
FIND spans 200+ experiences across 85+ destinations in 30+ countries, organized into three pillars:

- **FEEL** - emotionally and mentally restorative experiences: culturally immersive workshops, nature reconnection (open-air jungle safari at Alila Ubud), guided horseback rides with breath work.
- **FUEL** - culinary experiences: chef-led cooking sessions (a day with a chef at Thompson Madrid), tastings, personalized cocktail experiences at properties like Andaz Dubai The Palm.
- **FUNCTION** - active and adventure experiences designed to move your body and clear your head.

You can also browse by theme - arts, culture and community, exploration, and restoration. Specific listings rotate by destination and season.
how_it_works:
Fixed-price booking with points-or-cash flexibility. Every experience lists a set price, and you choose whether to pay with World of Hyatt points or cash - no bidding or auctions.

The earn angle is real: you collect 10 points per $1 spent on FIND experiences, plus a 20% bonus when you take points as your reward, plus tier-based and World of Hyatt Credit Card bonuses on top. So booking a paid experience also feeds your points balance.
how_to_access: Open to all World of Hyatt members - membership (free) is the only requirement to book. No elite tier or specific credit card is gated behind the platform. That said, elite tiers earn up to 30% additional bonus points, and holding the World of Hyatt Credit Card adds extra bonus points per dollar, so status and the card sweeten the earn side without being required to participate.
standout_examples: Real listings rotate, but recently featured examples give the flavor: a day cooking with chef Nino Redruello at Thompson Madrid; a personalized cocktail session with a mixologist at the rooftop bar of Andaz Dubai The Palm; an open-air jungle safari to reconnect with nature at Alila Ubud in Indonesia; and trail horseback riding with a stretch-and-ride breath-work program at Hyatt Regency Tamaya Resort and Spa in New Mexico. Inventory shifts by destination and season, so check the live platform for what is bookable now.
good_to_know: Cancellation policies differ per experience and are noted in each listing - some are fully non-refundable, so read the terms before you commit points or cash. Inventory is destination-specific (85+ destinations, 30+ countries), so availability depends heavily on where you are headed. Browse and book at experiences.hyatt.com or through the FIND section of World of Hyatt. Booking requires a (free) World of Hyatt account.
value_take: Worth knowing for the points-or-cash flexibility and the fact that paid bookings still earn World of Hyatt points - a rare double-dip. The wellbeing slant means genuine access (chef sessions, private nature experiences) rather than mass-market event tickets.

intro: Wyndham Rewards Experiences is the hotel program's entertainment portal, where your Wyndham points buy concert seats, festival passes, and sports tickets instead of free nights. It runs two ways: fixed-price "Redeem Now" tickets you grab outright, and live auctions where members bid points and the highest bid wins. Think of it as a second exit ramp for points you might otherwise sit on - no status or special card required.
what_you_get:
The lineup leans hard into live entertainment and sports:
- **Concerts** - big-name arena shows and Madison Square Garden runs (recent featured artists have included Harry Styles suite tickets, Phish, and Rush)
- **Music festivals** - full-weekend and VIP passes to events like Outside Lands, Ohana, and Shaky Knees
- **Sports** - MLB and Minor League Baseball ticket vouchers, plus PGA Tour access around the Wyndham Championship; past drops have included money-can't-buy extras like riding the Zamboni at a Rangers game
- **VIP and access perks** - backstage tours, suite seating, and merch bundles attached to select packages

Inventory is bundled into themed groups (for example "Music Festivals" or "Madison Square Garden Concerts") and rotates constantly.
how_it_works:
Two redemption mechanics, side by side:
- **Redeem Now (fixed price)** - a set point cost, guaranteed as long as it's in stock and you have the points. Fixed-point rewards start as low as 2,500 points.
- **Bid (auction)** - you bid points on a single package and the highest bid at close wins. Starting bids run roughly 20,000 to 100,000 points. You can set a confidential max bid and the system auto-bids for you in increments; points are only deducted if you win. An "Auto Bid Extend" feature pushes the close out five more minutes whenever a bid lands in the final five, so last-second sniping is blunted.

Short on points? Wyndham will nudge you to buy more - which is exactly when to slow down and do the math.
how_to_access: Open to any Wyndham Rewards member - no elite tier, co-brand card, or invite required. You just need a Wyndham Rewards account and enough points in it before you bid or redeem. Sign in at wyndhamrewardsexperiences.wyndhamrewards.com with your normal Wyndham Rewards credentials.
standout_examples: Recent featured drops have included Harry Styles suite tickets at Madison Square Garden, full-weekend and VIP passes to Outside Lands and Ohana music festivals, MSG concert runs for Phish and Rush, and a large batch of Minor League Baseball ticket vouchers tied to a summer promotion. The program has also surfaced genuine money-can't-buy items in the past, like VIP tickets to a sold-out Vans Warped Tour with a backstage tour, and riding the Zamboni at a New York Rangers home game. Specific inventory rotates - what's live this week won't be the same next month.
good_to_know: Auctions are binding - win the bid and the points come out of your account automatically, so don't bid on anything you wouldn't actually attend. Inventory is US-centric (events are overwhelmingly in the States) and changes weekly, so check back often and browse the "Featured Bundles" groupings to find what's live. Fixed-price items are first-come and can sell out. Refund and transfer terms are set per package in the portal's Terms & Conditions, and tickets are generally treated as final once redeemed - read the fine print on each listing before committing. Points can be purchased if you're short, but buying points to chase a redemption is rarely a good deal.
value_take: It's a legitimately useful escape hatch for Wyndham points, especially if you earn them faster than you burn them on hotels - the access angle (suites, festivals, VIP) and the points-or-bid flexibility are real. Just go in with a redemption you actually want, since auctions are binding and buying points to win one erodes the value fast.
refundable: Varies by package; tickets generally final
